text: APPROVE: Extracting the `#!` check into `IsInterpreterDirective` and returning `IsInterpreterDirective(line, i, prefix) ? -1 : i` keeps the logic identical (`-1` for a `#!` directive, otherwise `i`). The nested `if` (+3) and its `&&` sequence (+1) leave the method, while the new ternary adds +3, so the complexity drops from 16 to 15, which meets the threshold. The new helper is used, and passing `line` into a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` parameter should compile cleanly, so I don't expect new warnings. I judged this from the diff alone and did not build the project or run the analyzer.
